items.q: Small family firms often weather a recession because their staff stand by them ______, even when wages are paid late.
items.vi: Các doanh nghiệp gia đình nhỏ thường vượt qua suy thoái vì nhân viên sát cánh cùng họ dù sướng hay khổ, ngay cả khi lương bị trả chậm.
items.explanation: Idiom of loyalty: stand by them … even when wages are paid late means staying loyal in good times and bad, so through thick and thin (= loyally, whatever happens) fits. ✗ by hook or by crook — by any means possible; ✗ by leaps and bounds — very quickly (of progress); ✗ at sixes and sevens — in total confusion.

items.q: Setting up two-factor authentication turned out to be ______ — the whole process took less than a minute.
items.vi: Hóa ra việc cài đặt xác thực hai lớp dễ như ăn kẹo — toàn bộ quá trình chưa đến một phút.
items.explanation: Idiom for ease: took less than a minute shows the task was very easy, so a piece of cake (= something very easy) fits. ✗ a hard nut to crack — a difficult problem, the opposite; ✗ a storm in a teacup — a big fuss about nothing; ✗ a drop in the ocean — a tiny, unimportant amount.

items.q: Data brokers can ______ a user's home address from nothing more than a handful of location pings.
items.vi: Các công ty môi giới dữ liệu có thể xác định chính xác địa chỉ nhà của người dùng chỉ từ vài tín hiệu định vị.
items.explanation: Word choice: finding a user's home address from … a handful of location pings is locating something exactly, so pinpoint (= identify precisely) fits. ✗ overlook — fail to notice, the opposite; ✗ survey — look over a wide area generally; ✗ browse — look through casually, without a target.

items.q: When the regulator rejected the trial data, the research team found itself ______, with three years of work to repeat.
items.vi: Khi cơ quan quản lý bác bỏ dữ liệu thử nghiệm, nhóm nghiên cứu thấy mình phải bắt đầu lại từ đầu, với ba năm công sức phải làm lại.
items.explanation: Idiom for lost progress: three years of work to repeat means starting again from the beginning, so back to square one fits. ✗ on the same page — in agreement with others; ✗ out of the woods — safe, past the danger; ✗ in the same boat — in the same difficult situation as someone else.

items.q: The auditors spent three weeks ______ over the bank's ledgers before the missing transfers came to light.
items.vi: Các kiểm toán viên mất ba tuần nghiền ngẫm sổ sách của ngân hàng trước khi các khoản chuyển tiền thất thoát bị phát hiện.
items.explanation: Word choice with over: three weeks … over the bank's ledgers is careful, lengthy study, so poring over (= studying closely) fits. ✗ peering — looking with difficulty, takes at, not over; ✗ gazing — looking steadily for a long time, takes at; ✗ squinting — narrowing the eyes to see, takes at.

items.q: The surgeon was confident the patient would pull ______, though recovery ______ such an operation can take months.
items.vi: Bác sĩ phẫu thuật tin rằng bệnh nhân sẽ qua khỏi, dù việc hồi phục sau một ca mổ như vậy có thể mất nhiều tháng.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb + preposition: the patient would pull through = survive a serious operation, and the noun recovery takes from (recovery from an operation). ✗ over / of — pull over = stop a car; recovery of = getting something back; ✗ out / in — pull out = withdraw; recovery in = improvement in a market; ✗ off / to — pull off = succeed in something difficult; recovery to is not used.

items.q: Company spokespeople tried to ______ the scale of the breach, insisting only a handful of accounts had been exposed.
items.vi: Người phát ngôn của công ty cố giảm nhẹ mức độ của vụ rò rỉ, khăng khăng rằng chỉ một số ít tài khoản bị lộ.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb: insisting only a handful of accounts had been exposed shows they made the breach seem smaller, so play down (= minimise) fits. ✗ play up — exaggerate, the opposite; ✗ play off — set two people against each other; ✗ play along — pretend to agree or cooperate.

items.q: Despite objections from privacy groups, the ministry has decided to ______ with the facial-recognition scheme in every station.
items.vi: Bất chấp sự phản đối của các nhóm bảo vệ quyền riêng tư, bộ đã quyết định xúc tiến kế hoạch nhận diện khuôn mặt ở mọi nhà ga.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb with with: Despite objections … has decided to … with the scheme means continuing regardless, so press ahead with (= go on determinedly) fits. ✗ press for — demand something, and cannot take with; ✗ press upon — force something on someone; ✗ get ahead — advance in a career, not used with a plan.

items.q: The merger is still ______ in the air, so the bank has put its hiring plans ______ hold.
items.vi: Vụ sáp nhập vẫn còn chưa ngã ngũ, nên ngân hàng đã tạm hoãn kế hoạch tuyển dụng.
items.explanation: Two fixed expressions: up in the air = still undecided, and put … on hold = postponed. ✗ out / in — out in the air and in hold are not expressions; ✗ off / at — off in the air is not an expression, and at hold does not exist; ✗ over / under — over in the air is not an expression; under hold is not used for postponing.

items.q: Economists warn that ______ inflation is quietly eroding the value of household savings.
items.vi: Các nhà kinh tế cảnh báo rằng lạm phát dai dẳng đang âm thầm bào mòn giá trị tiền tiết kiệm của các hộ gia đình.
items.explanation: Collocation: inflation that is quietly eroding … savings over time is persistent inflation (= continuing stubbornly). ✗ insistent — demanding attention, used of people or voices; ✗ resistant — needs to (resistant to change) and describes what resists, not what continues; ✗ consistent — steady and unchanging, not stubbornly lasting.

items.q: The two governments reached a tariff deal ______, only minutes before the new duties were due to take effect.
options: at the end of the day
items.vi: Hai chính phủ đạt được thỏa thuận thuế quan vào phút chót, chỉ vài phút trước khi các mức thuế mới có hiệu lực.
items.explanation: Idiom of time: only minutes before the new duties were due to take effect means at the last possible moment, so at the eleventh hour fits. ✗ at the end of the day — ultimately, when everything is considered; ✗ around the clock — all day and all night; ✗ in the long run — over a long period, eventually.

items.q: The health ministry has ______ a thorough investigation into hygiene standards at the private clinic.
items.vi: Bộ Y tế đã tiến hành một cuộc điều tra kỹ lưỡng về tiêu chuẩn vệ sinh tại phòng khám tư đó.
items.explanation: Verb + noun collocation: with a thorough investigation the verb is conduct (also carry out / hold). ✗ made — make goes with a decision or an effort, not an investigation; ✗ done — do goes with research or homework, not an investigation; ✗ taken — take goes with action or a decision, not an investigation.

items.q: Regulators fined the platform for failing to obtain ______ consent before selling users' browsing histories to advertisers.
items.vi: Cơ quan quản lý đã phạt nền tảng này vì không xin được sự đồng ý có hiểu biết của người dùng trước khi bán lịch sử duyệt web của họ cho các nhà quảng cáo.
items.explanation: Fixed collocation: consent before selling users' browsing histories is the legal idea of agreement given with full knowledge, so informed consent fits. ✗ knowing — describes a person or look (a knowing smile), not consent; ✗ advised — means recommended and does not pair with consent; ✗ aware — describes a person (aware of), never a noun like consent.

items.q: Ministers insist the economy is recovering, ______ most households report that their real incomes have fallen.
items.vi: Các bộ trưởng khẳng định nền kinh tế đang hồi phục, trong khi hầu hết các hộ gia đình cho biết thu nhập thực tế của họ đã giảm.
items.explanation: Linking word: Ministers insist … recovering versus most households report … fallen are two contrasting clauses, so whereas (= while, by contrast) fits. ✗ despite — a preposition, needs a noun or -ing form, not a full clause; ✗ otherwise — means if not, which makes no sense here; ✗ so that — expresses purpose, but falling incomes are not the ministers' aim.

items.q: After a decade in investment banking, she found it hard to get used to ______ on a researcher's salary.
items.vi: Sau mười năm làm ngân hàng đầu tư, cô thấy khó mà quen được với việc sống bằng đồng lương của một nhà nghiên cứu.
items.explanation: Gerund after a preposition: in get used to, to is a preposition, so the verb takes -ing: living. ✗ live — a bare infinitive cannot follow a preposition; ✗ to live — doubles the to (used to to live); ✗ having lived — a perfect gerund refers to a finished past action, but she is adjusting to a present situation.

items.q: The board recommended that the chief executive ______ from any decision involving her family's shareholding.
items.vi: Hội đồng quản trị đề nghị giám đốc điều hành không tham gia bất kỳ quyết định nào liên quan đến cổ phần của gia đình bà.
items.explanation: Subjunctive: after recommended that, the verb takes the base form: abstain, regardless of the subject or the past tense of the main clause. ✗ abstains — present -s form, not the subjunctive; ✗ abstained — past tense describes what happened, not what was recommended; ✗ will abstain — future form is not used in a that-clause after recommend.

items.q: ______ for the central bank's emergency intervention, the currency would have collapsed within days.
items.vi: Nếu không có sự can thiệp khẩn cấp của ngân hàng trung ương, đồng tiền này đã sụp đổ chỉ trong vài ngày.
items.explanation: Inverted third conditional: would have collapsed marks an unreal past, and Had it not been for = If it had not been for; the auxiliary had moves before the subject and not stays after it. ✗ Had not it been — not cannot come between the auxiliary and the subject when uncontracted; ✗ It had not been — no inversion and no if, so it is not a condition; ✗ Not had it been — not cannot begin the inversion.

items.q: Only after the second wave of infections ______ the true cost of years of underfunding the health service.
items.vi: Chỉ sau làn sóng lây nhiễm thứ hai công chúng mới nhận ra cái giá thực sự của nhiều năm cắt giảm ngân sách y tế.
items.explanation: Inversion after a negative/restrictive opener: Only after + phrase at the start forces auxiliary + subject + bare verb in the main clause: did the public realise. ✗ the public realised — normal word order is not allowed after Only after; ✗ the public did realise — did must come before the subject, not after; ✗ realised the public — the full verb cannot invert; an auxiliary is needed.

items.q: Without her glasses, the pharmacist had to ______ at the tiny print on the label to read the dosage.
items.vi: Không có kính, dược sĩ phải nheo mắt nhìn kỹ dòng chữ li ti trên nhãn để đọc liều dùng.
items.explanation: Word choice with at: Without her glasses … the tiny print means looking closely at something hard to see, so peer at fits. ✗ gaze — look steadily and dreamily, not with effort; ✗ glare — look angrily at someone; ✗ observe — watch carefully, takes a direct object without at.

items.q: Journalists eventually ______ the leaked memo to a contractor working for the health ministry.
items.vi: Cuối cùng các nhà báo đã lần ra bản ghi nhớ bị rò rỉ xuất phát từ một nhà thầu làm việc cho Bộ Y tế.
items.explanation: Word choice with to: following the memo to a contractor means finding its source, so traced … to (= followed evidence back to its origin) fits. ✗ spotted — noticed suddenly, not followed to a source; ✗ sighted — saw with the eyes, used of ships or animals; ✗ located — found the position of, does not take to a source.

items.q: It's high time regulators ______ a clear line between targeted advertising and outright surveillance.
items.vi: Đã đến lúc các cơ quan quản lý phải vạch ra ranh giới rõ ràng giữa quảng cáo nhắm mục tiêu và giám sát trắng trợn.
items.explanation: Past subjunctive after It's high time: the expression takes a past form to say something should already be happening: drew. ✗ draw — present or base form is not used after It's high time + subject; ✗ will draw — future form is not used after this expression; ✗ have drawn — a perfect form describes a completed action, but the line has not been drawn yet.

items.q: ______ research has been done on how late-night scrolling affects teenagers' sleep, so no one can yet say whether the harm is real.
items.vi: Rất ít nghiên cứu được thực hiện về việc lướt điện thoại khuya ảnh hưởng thế nào đến giấc ngủ của thanh thiếu niên, nên chưa ai dám nói tác hại đó là có thật.
items.explanation: Quantifier with an uncountable noun: research is uncountable and no one can yet say shows the amount is almost none, so Little (= hardly any) fits. ✗ A little — means some, enough to matter, which clashes with no one can yet say; ✗ Few — used only with plural countable nouns; ✗ A few — also for plural countable nouns, and means some.

items.q: The patient ______ the wrong dose — the pharmacy's records show every prescription that day was filled correctly.
items.vi: Bệnh nhân không thể nào đã bị đưa sai liều — hồ sơ nhà thuốc cho thấy mọi đơn thuốc hôm đó đều được cấp phát đúng.
items.explanation: Modal of deduction: records show every prescription … was filled correctly is evidence that it did NOT happen, so can't have been given (= I am sure it did not happen) fits. ✗ shouldn't have been given — criticises something that did happen; ✗ needn't have been given — says it happened but was unnecessary; ✗ mustn't have been given — must have is used for positive deduction only; the negative deduction is can't have.

items.q: ______ the sheer volume of records exposed in the breach, investigators expect the inquiry to take at least a year.
items.vi: Xét đến khối lượng hồ sơ bị lộ quá lớn trong vụ rò rỉ, các điều tra viên dự đoán cuộc điều tra sẽ kéo dài ít nhất một năm.
items.explanation: Participle preposition: Given + noun phrase means considering, taking into account, so Given the sheer volume of records introduces the reason for the year-long inquiry. ✗ Giving — a present participle would mean the investigators are giving the records; ✗ Give — a bare imperative cannot introduce a noun phrase as a reason; ✗ To give — an infinitive of purpose, but expecting a long inquiry is not done in order to give records.

items.q: Most users simply ______ the headlines in their news feed rather than read a single article to the end.
items.vi: Hầu hết người dùng chỉ lướt qua các tiêu đề trong bảng tin thay vì đọc trọn vẹn dù chỉ một bài báo.
items.explanation: Word choice with a direct object: the headlines … rather than read a single article to the end means reading quickly for the gist, so skim fits and takes the object directly. ✗ stare — look fixedly, needs at; ✗ gaze — look steadily and admiringly, needs at; ✗ squint — narrow the eyes to see, needs at.
